title: 10 Best Chocolate Shops in Bruges
description: The best chocolate shops in Bruges, Belgium — curated from hundreds of Reddit reviews. Artisanal pralines, truffles, hot chocolate & more. Interactive map included.

places.name: The Chocolate Line
places.verdict: The most polarizing chocolatier in Belgium.

comparison.best for: Creative Pralines in Simon Stevinplein 19 with a €35–60/box spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.6★ from 4,415 Google reviews · Creative Pralines · Simon Stevinplein 19
comparison.why it made the list: The most polarizing chocolatier in Belgium. Half of Reddit calls it the best in the world; the other half calls it an overpriced tourist trap. The truth: Persoone’s wild flavors are genuinely creative and well-executed, but you’re paying a premium for the brand. Worth visiting for the experience — just know that quieter shops nearby may offer better value per praline.

places.name: Chocolatier Dumon

comparison.best for: Family Artisan in Eiermarkt 6 (flagship) & Simon Stevinplein with a €25–45/box spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.2★ from 734 Google reviews · Family Artisan · Eiermarkt 6 (flagship) & Simon Stevinplein
comparison.why it made the list: The people’s champion. Dumon is the shop Belgian locals recommend most consistently — a multi-generational family business that’s been handmaking chocolate in Bruges for over 30 years. No gimmicks, no wild flavors — just exceptionally well-made traditional Belgian pralines. The flagship store has a charming, old-world feel. If you only visit one shop, make it this one.

places.name: Depla Chocolaterie

comparison.best for: Artisanal Truffles in Mariastraat 20 with a €20–40/box spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.5★ from 514 Google reviews · Artisanal Truffles · Mariastraat 20
comparison.limitations: chocolate professionals and Belgian locals rate it among the very best
comparison.why it made the list: The connoisseur’s pick. Depla flies under the tourist radar on a quieter side street, but chocolate professionals and Belgian locals rate it among the very best. Pol Depla’s pure truffles are “absolute top” — rich, delicate, and handmade in tiny batches. The shop itself is small and unassuming, which is exactly the point.

places.name: Pralinette

comparison.best for: Pralines & Workshop in Wollestraat 31B with a €25–50/box · Workshops from €40 spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.5★ from 312 Google reviews · Pralines & Workshop · Wollestraat 31B
comparison.why it made the list: The complete package. Master chocolatier Fangio De Baets handmakes everything on-site, and the quality is excellent. But the real draw is the hidden terrace overlooking a canal — arguably the most beautiful chocolate-drinking spot in Bruges. The workshop is genuinely fun and informative. Book ahead.

places.name: Chocolaterie Spegelaere

comparison.best for: Traditional Family in Ezelstraat 92 with a €20–40/box spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.8★ from 344 Google reviews · Traditional Family · Ezelstraat 92
comparison.why it made the list: The heritage pick. Spegelaere has the longest family chocolate tradition in Bruges — and that’s saying something in a city defined by chocolate. Located on the charming Ezelstraat (away from the main tourist drag), this tiny shop makes everything by hand using recipes passed down through generations. Their marzipan grape cluster is iconic.

places.name: BbyB Chocolates

comparison.best for: Designer Pralines in Sint-Amandsstraat 39 with a €35–55/box spend range
comparison.strengths: 5★ from 2 Google reviews · Designer Pralines · Sint-Amandsstraat 39
comparison.why it made the list: The Apple Store of chocolate. BbyB’s minimalist branding, numbered flavors, and color-coded families feel almost tech-forward — but the chocolate is seriously good. Born from a beloved Bruges restaurant (Bartholomew’s), each praline is a design object. Pricey, but the packaging and quality justify it for a special gift.

places.name: Chocolaterie Sukerbuyc
places.verdict: One of Bruges’ oldest chocolatiers, and one of the few that still makes everything from scratch in their own atelier.

comparison.best for: Handmade Artisan in Katelijnestraat 5 with a €20–40/box spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.4★ from 345 Google reviews · Handmade Artisan · Katelijnestraat 5
comparison.why it made the list: One of Bruges’ oldest chocolatiers, and one of the few that still makes everything from scratch in their own atelier. Sukerbuyc stays true to time-honored techniques while embracing new flavors. The Katelijnestraat location is slightly off the main tourist circuit, which means fewer crowds and more genuine conversation with the chocolatiers.

places.name: Chocolatier Van Oost
places.verdict: A Bruges institution that’s been making pralines steps from the Belfry for over four decades.

comparison.best for: Classic Pralines in Wollestraat 11 (near the Belfry) with a €20–40/box spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.6★ from 121 Google reviews · Classic Pralines · Wollestraat 11 (near the Belfry)
comparison.why it made the list: A Bruges institution that’s been making pralines steps from the Belfry for over four decades. Van Oost doesn’t chase trends — they perfect classics. The praliné and gianduja fillings are textbook Belgian, and the ginger truffles add a modern twist. Conveniently located but still genuinely artisanal.

places.name: The Old Chocolate House
places.verdict: Not a shop for buying boxes — this is where you sit down and drink chocolate.

comparison.best for: Hot Chocolate in Mariastraat 1 with a €5–8 per cup spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.5★ from 2,941 Google reviews · Hot Chocolate · Mariastraat 1
comparison.limitations: nowhere to get a proper hot chocolate
comparison.why it made the list: Not a shop for buying boxes — this is where you sit down and drink chocolate. The concept is brilliant: boiling milk + a stick of real chocolate + you melt it yourself. It started around 2008 when the owners realized Bruges had hundreds of chocolate shops but nowhere to get a proper hot chocolate. The tearoom upstairs is cozy. Perfect for a cold Bruges afternoon.

places.name: Choco-Story Museum
places.verdict: Not a chocolate shop, but the best way to understand why Belgian chocolate matters.

comparison.best for: Museum & Tasting in Wijnzakstraat 2 with a €12 admission spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.1★ from 9,032 Google reviews · Museum & Tasting · Wijnzakstraat 2
comparison.limitations: the best way to understand why Belgian chocolate matters
comparison.why it made the list: Not a chocolate shop, but the best way to understand why Belgian chocolate matters. The history tour is genuinely interesting (Aztec cacao rituals to Belgian praline invention), the live demonstrations are engaging, and the tastings are generous. Open daily 10am–6pm. A great first stop — you’ll appreciate the craftsmanship more at every shop after this.
